title: Analysis of canonical and non-canonical splice sites in mammalian genomes
authors: Burset M, Seledtsov IA, Solovyev VV
population: 43,337 splice-site pairs of mammalian genes annotated in GenBank (InfoGene database), 22,489 of them supported by expressed sequence tags
funder: This work was supported by the Wellcome Trust grant to V.S. and grant FPI95 from Ministerio de Educación y Ciencia to M.B.
authorConflicts: None stated. The work was done at the Sanger Centre; the corresponding author's present address is given as EOS Biotechnology, South San Francisco.
result: Of 22,489 EST-supported mammalian splice-site pairs, 98.71% had the canonical dinucleotides GT at the donor and AG at the acceptor site and 0.56% were GC-AG; after correction with human genomic sequence the authors estimate 99.24% GT-AG, 0.69% GC-AG, 0.05% AT-AC and 0.02% other pairs. Introns flanked by GT-AG are excised from pre-mRNA by the spliceosome containing the U1, U2, U4/U6 and U5 snRNPs; AT-AC introns by a spliceosome of U11, U12, U4atac/U6atac and U5 snRNPs.
